text:
[NLFC.3.3] Constraints:

- **Pump is the only writer.** Do not call `ds_engine_*` functions
  concurrently on the same engine from multiple threads. libds does not lock;
  the integrator serialises externally. Concurrent pump + assert on one engine
  is undefined behaviour.
- **Multiple engines in different threads is fine** — each is independent.
- **Do not block inside callbacks.** Callbacks fire on the pump thread; a
  blocking callback blocks the pump. Push discovered work onto a queue the
  runtime services later.
- **Do not call back into the engine that called you.** A callback holds a
  live handle and runs on the pump's stack, so re-entry is easy to write by
  accident; every `ds_engine_*` call on **that** engine returns
  `DS_ERR_STATE` ([RARC.13.16]). This covers reads as well as writes — a read
  mid-pump is a torn snapshot. The same holds inside the callback an
  enumerating read invokes once per item, such as `ds_engine_for_each_fact`'s
  visitor ([RARC.13.17]). Calling into a **different** engine is the intended
  cross-tier pattern and is fine.

tla.name: nlfc_3_3__InputAssert
tla.note: The integrator's assert, between pumps by its guard: the exclusion this clause makes the integrator's duty, assumed, as [RARC.13.16] says its model assumes it. pump_single_writer.tla is where the exclusion is checked.
